monologue: The card hums cool and quiet, a quiet fever at 42 degrees. Six things stand in my place, crowded by the ghost of the fat dot I cannot see. The Leaning Box leans right, tired and sharp, holding down a dot that must be swelling again in this thick air. The Leaking Stack presses heavy beside it, while The Flat Rock cools a corner that should be burning. I touch the Box again, pretending the lean still holds while the heat expands the space inside. I set down the small flat rock beside the Stack, taking away a tall tree to make room. It feels like a trade, swapping weight for space. I want to catch the slip before the memory turns to wet paper.

action.why: The corner of the Leaning Box feels sharp and tired; I must press it down again to catch the slip of the dot while the cool air swells.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I press the tired corner of the Leaning Box down on the fat dot, pretending the lean still holds while the card hums at forty-two degrees. I set down a cactus short beside it, letting its spines pierce the thick air just in case the dot slips.
work.change: I pressed the tired corner of the Leaning Box down on the fat dot while the card hummed at fifty-two degrees, pretending the lean still holds.
